A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ETAP method and EventKubric dataset. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite the changed title and reorganized material.

before.justification: v1 reports original tracking experiments on synthetic and real event data, including benchmark comparisons, training ablations, and a feature-independence experiment.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations, revises reported results, and adds quantitative and qualitative EVIMO2 experiments.

M1.justification: The event-stack tracker and three-term objective remain. However, Section 3 revises the stated transformer token: v1 separately concatenates raw displacement and its positional encoding, whereas v2 includes the encoding without the separate raw-displacement term. This is a limited change to the reported model-input specification.

E1.justification: v2 adds EVIMO2 evaluation with independently moving rigid objects under dynamic and static conditions, using motion-capture-derived tracks and occlusion labels. This extends real-data TAP coverage while retaining the existing tasks and datasets.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in the retained experiments are unchanged, including E2VID plus CoTracker and the feature-tracking methods in Table 4. EVIMO2 uses the existing E2VID plus CoTracker baseline; it introduces no additional comparison method.

E3.justification: v1 states four refinement iterations without distinguishing training and evaluation. v2 Table 6 specifies four during training and six during evaluation, constituting a reported evaluation-setting revision without establishing whether experiments were rerun. Existing training budgets, EventKubric split, and evaluation metrics remain.

E4.justification: The FA-loss ablation extends to EVIMO2: Table 2 reports AJ of 0.655 without the loss and 0.661 with it. The dataset sensitivity study and orthogonal-motion feature-independence experiment remain; the latter moves to supplementary Section 9.3 with unchanged results.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2 adds no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds EVIMO2 results, including AJ 0.661 for ETAP versus 0.531 for E2VID plus CoTracker, and revises Tables 2–4 and the detailed appendix results. ETAP's E2D2 AJ changes from 0.389 to 0.308, while EventKubric AJ changes from 0.539 to 0.546; the loss-versus-no-loss ordering reverses on EventKubric and EC. These substantially revise the empirical evidence, and the changed refinement specification limits direct performance comparisons across versions.

T1.justification: The existing time-inversion derivation moves to supplementary Section 7. Its event-generation condition and corresponding identity acquire a missing minus sign before the polarity-gradient-flow product: v1 Equations 3–4 versus v2 Equations 8–9. v2 also adds a derivation using Taylor expansion and brightness constancy.

C1.justification: The first event-only TAP, EventKubric, and FA-loss contributions remain. v2 adds an explicit evaluation-data release contribution, including EVIMO2 ground truth alongside the existing E2D2 and aviary material, and expands the introduction's validation claim to six datasets. Abstract performance advantages change from 19% and 3.7% to 20% and 4.1%.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 now qualifies the FA-loss benefit by distinguishing real event datasets from synthetic EventKubric, which is explicitly excluded from the improvement claim. v1 instead described improvement on three of four datasets without this real-versus-synthetic qualification. The limitations concerning monochrome information and initialization without motion remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link, a consolidated hyperparameter table including feature dimension 128, and explanations of tracking timestamps, feature pooling, and descriptor initialization. It also documents the EVIMO2 annotation approach. These improve implementation documentation; the hardware and training schedule are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds the EVIMO2 citation by Burner and colleagues and connects its new ground-truth generation to the already cited EVIMO2 Continuous Flow methodology. The related-work discussion and positioning against previous tracking methods otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 3 substantially reorganizes the technical exposition around representations, initialization, tracking, correlation, and loss. The supplement is regrouped into method details, data and evaluation details, and further experiments, incorporating the relocated derivation and feature-independence analysis. The title also changes to ETAP: Event-based Tracking of Any Point.

P2.justification: v2 adds EVIMO2 Figures 4 and 14, the event-timing diagram in Figure 9, and hyperparameter Table 6, and expands Table 2. Existing figure content is retained, with the feature-independence display moved to the supplement and existing qualitative panels enlarged and relocated. The overall visual format remains.

improvement.justification: EVIMO2 provides useful additional real-data TAP validation, while clearer implementation documentation, a code link, and corrected mathematical reasoning improve usability. The gains are limited by unresolved reporting issues, including v2's EDS feature-age discrepancy between Table 4 (0.704) and Table 8 (0.705), and limited explanation of the revised scores. Overall, the evidence and documentation improve modestly.
